message.content:
To terminate Visual Studio Code (the main executable is **code.exe**) from a Windows command prompt or PowerShell, you can use the built‑in `taskkill` utility:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

**Explanation**

| Argument | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `/IM`    | Specifies the image name (process name) – here we target `code.exe`. |
| `/F`     | Forces termination (`/T` would also terminate child processes). |

If you run this from an elevated (Administrator) command prompt, it will forcefully stop the VS Code process even if it’s hung.

---

### Using PowerShell

PowerShell offers a more idiomatic way:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or, if you prefer the same syntax as `taskkill`:

```powershell
Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force
```

Both commands do essentially the same thing—forcefully end the `code.exe` process.

---

### Things to keep in mind

1. **Multiple instances**  
   VS Code may spawn helper processes (e.g., extensions, background tasks). Killing just `code.exe` stops the main window but may leave orphaned child processes. Adding `/T` to `taskkill` (`taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T`) will also terminate those children.

2. **Unsaved work**  
   Force‑killing will discard any unsaved changes. Use it only when the application is unresponsive.

3. **Permissions**  
   If you’re not running as Administrator, `taskkill` may refuse to terminate processes owned by other users. In that case, elevate your console or use PowerShell’s `Start-Process` with `-Verb RunAs`.

That’s all you need to quickly shut down VS Code from the command line!
